title: 5 Best Bookshop Cafés in Samcheong-dong
description: The best bookshop cafés in Samcheong-dong & Bukchon, Seoul — curated from Reddit reviews and travel blogs. Hanok book cafés, mountain retreats & literary hideaways.

places.name: BooksCooks (북스쿡스)

redditQuotes.text: We recommend BooksCooks, where you can dine surrounded by walls of cookbooks and literature in a beautifully renovated hanok.
The decor is very unique, incorporating a bit of vintage and modern in a renovated hanok — very cute and cozy, but surprisingly roomy inside.

places.verdict: Tucked into the alleys of Bukchon Hanok Village, BooksCooks is the kind of place you stumble upon and immediately fall in love with.

places.name: Dae-o Bookstore (대오서점)

redditQuotes.text: I went to Namjoon (RM from BTS)'s favourite bookstore café, Dae-o Bookstore in Seoul. It's been open since 1951 and it's magical.

places.verdict: Seoul's oldest bookstore, open since 1951, sits in the heart of Seochon — a 10-minute walk from Samcheong-dong through Gyeongbokgung.

comparison.why it made the list: Seoul's oldest bookstore, open since 1951, sits in the heart of Seochon — a 10-minute walk from Samcheong-dong through Gyeongbokgung. Cash only, tiny, and gloriously unchanged. BTS's RM made it famous internationally, but locals have loved it for decades. The café extension adds just enough comfort without disturbing the old-world charm. Open daily 12:00–21:00.

The real draw is the atmosphere — shelves packed with secondhand Korean literature, faded covers, and decades of literary history.

places.name: The Forest Chosochaekbang (더숲 초소책방)

redditQuotes.text: The Forest Chosochaekbang is housed in a former security guard post on Inwangsan Mountain. Glass walls, floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, panoramic city views. One of the most unique cafés in Seoul.

places.verdict: A former police guard post reborn as a glass-walled book sanctuary on Inwangsan Mountain.

comparison.best for: Mountain Book Café in 172 Inwangsan-ro, Jongno-gu with a ₩6,000–₩12,000 spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.4★ from 1,316 Google reviews · Mountain Book Café · 172 Inwangsan-ro, Jongno-gu
comparison.why it made the list: A former police guard post reborn as a glass-walled book sanctuary on Inwangsan Mountain. The 20-minute uphill walk from Gyeongbokgung through Seochon village is part of the experience — you'll pass Tongin Market and the Yun Dong-ju Literature Museum. Specializes in environmental literature and hosts intimate book talks and music concerts. Worth the climb.
comparison.what to order: The Forest Chosochaekbang (더숲 초소책방), a mountain book café located at 172 Inwangsan-ro, Jongno-gu, offers a N/A-priced experience. For the best experience, order the signature Ang butter croissant (red bean and butter) with artisanal coffee. Grab a book on environmental topics from their curated collection and sit by the glass walls overlooking Seoul.

places.name: Café Yeon (카페 연)

redditQuotes.text: Yeon is the hippie café where the servers don't wear shoes even in the dead of winter and the interior has a traditional hanok style, but like it has been refinished and repainted for modern times. The entire place induces a calming sigh. It's a bit of peace in the hectic world of Seoul.

places.verdict: Not a traditional bookshop café, but Café Yeon belongs on this list for its literary atmosphere and zen-like reading vibe.

This is what slow travel feels like.
